card.name: Plasma protein binding and displacement statements
card.fires_on: Words inside sentences about a drug's binding to plasma proteins or displacing other drugs from binding sites, such as 'is', 'not', 'no', 'from' or the end of a drug name. It fires in protein binding or drug interaction sections.

modes.label: Verb or link word in binding statement
modes.description: A small word like 'is', 'not', 'no', 'can' or 'from' right after a drug name in a sentence about protein binding or displacement.
modes.example: The in vitro binding of olanzapine and fluoxetine capsules to human plasma proteins<< is>> similar to the individual components.

modes.label: Drug name ending in binding context
modes.description: The last piece of a drug name such as buspirone at the start of an in vitro protein binding statement.
modes.example: In vitro , buspir<<one>> does not displace tightly bound drugs like

modes.label: Numbers and brackets after bound
modes.description: A word or bracket right before a percent-bound value for plasma protein binding.
modes.example: Ketorolac is highly bound to human plasma protein (<<mean>> 99.2%).

card.writes: No clear output effect; it mildly suppresses words about activity and activation.
card.plain: It marks sentences that say how strongly a drug sticks to blood proteins or pushes other drugs off them.
